description:
## Why

PKIX-xj81 decomposition, pattern 6 of 6. Audit notes that the builder cycle
guard is correct but is only stress-tested via the 30-self-loop budget test
— not a true 3-cycle A->B->C->A. This bead adds direct coverage.

## What

Pool topology:

```
LoopCertA: subject=CN=A, issuer=CN=C, signed-by=C-key, AKI=C-key-SKI
LoopCertB: subject=CN=B, issuer=CN=A, signed-by=A-key, AKI=A-key-SKI
LoopCertC: subject=CN=C, issuer=CN=B, signed-by=B-key, AKI=B-key-SKI
```

The signatures form a closed loop: A is issued by C, B by A, C by B. No
trust anchor reachable from this pool.

Build steps:

1. Generator issues three DER fixtures. Note: openssl normally rejects
   non-self-signed root issuance because there is no anchor; the generator
   has to bypass standard CA setup and just produce three certificates that
   reference each other. May need direct ASN.1 construction or carefully
   ordered signing of partial certs. Document the technique in the
   generator script.
2. Test (`tests/cycle_loop.rs`):
   - Pool: all three LoopCert*.
   - Trust anchors: empty (or unrelated).
   - `build_path(&LoopCertA, &pool, &anchors)` must return `Err(...)` with
     either `MaxDepthExceeded`, `CycleDetected`, or `NoPathFound` —
     whichever variant the builder uses. Document the chosen verdict.
   - The call must return promptly (assert with a timeout < 5s, sanity
     check) and must NOT exhaust the candidate budget — the cycle guard
     should terminate before reaching `PathBuilderConfig::max_candidates`.
3. Negative: do the same with a 2-cycle (A->B->A, two-cert) to confirm
   the simpler case also terminates.

## Acceptance

- [ ] At least three DER fixtures committed.
- [ ] Generation reproducible (may require a small Rust program emitted
      by `generate.sh`, since openssl CLI cannot easily produce loop chains).
- [ ] One integration test verifying loop termination.

## Depends on

PKIX-xj81.1.
title: pkix-path-builder: 3-cycle A->B->C->A loop guard fixture+test
